headline: Red Wings' Michal Postava a winner in first career NHL start
take:
Per ESPN, Michal Postava made his first career NHL start a winning one, backstopping the Red Wings to a shootout win over the Oilers.

The goalie numbers are thin, so treat them gently. Postava stopped 87.5 percent of shots in his one game so far this season, and our goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie prevented compared with an average one facing the same shots) put him at -0.01, essentially dead even. He wasn't the reason DET won, and he didn't cost them either. He came up as a free agent who was never drafted, after posting a .937 save percentage over 25 AHL games for the Grand Rapids Griffins in 2025-26. The team picture is more interesting. DET sits at 4-4-3 but controls 52.2 percent of expected goals, a measure of chance quality, and has been 7.9 goals worse than expected in finishing, which points to bad luck more than bad play. EDM is 8-2-1 on 14.1 goals above expected, and their goalies have been 8.7 goals below expected, so that record rests on shaky ground.
